what_happened.summary: It makes sense he feels scared after being hit a few times and going hitless. Those moments are information about his approach, not a measure of his value. The one focus this week is building confidence at the plate before worrying about hits.

output.call_type_rationale: This is purely a player development question about rebuilding confidence and addressing fear at the plate — no umpire judgment or rule application is involved.

channel.who: The head coach, with the player one-on-one.
channel.how: Talk calmly after practice or between innings, ask how he feels, remind him you believe in him, and shift attention to being ready and his approach rather than the result.

output.teachable_moment: His worth isn't tied to hits or hit-by-pitches, and your belief in him matters more than his stat line. When he sees you believe before he does, confidence can grow.

individual: Pick one controllable to grade after each at-bat, such as 'Was I ready?' or 'Did I swing at my pitch?'
Practise plate coverage or a two-strike approach this week, one thing at a time
Use a calm breathing routine before stepping in to reset fear and focus
team: Run soft-toss or short-distance BP where hitters can succeed and build trust
Praise effort and process, not hits, in front of the team
Keep the mood fun and low-pressure so he wants to keep stepping up
at_home: Let him talk first about the game and listen without fixing
Praise his effort and attitude, not whether he got a hit
Leave batting technique to the coach and bring it up at a calm, agreed time

output.focus: Build confidence at the plate before results

life_lesson.text: Players rise to the belief adults show in them, on the diamond and later at school, work and home. Remind him that who he is matters far more than today's box score.

lessons.title: Believe in your players before they believe in themselves
lessons.principle: Have confidence in your players even when they don't show it, even when their track record says failure. Don't lose that confidence. Feed it to them and they will succeed.

lessons.title: Your value isn't your stat line
lessons.principle: Your value is not determined by your failures or your successes.
